5 Questions Every Accredited Investor Should Ask Before Investing in Oil and Gas

5 Questions Every Accredited Investor Should Ask Before Investing in Oil and Gas

PR Newswire

HOUSTON, Nov. 5, 2026

Wheeler Resource Recovery President Kevin K. Thibeau shares what investors should understand before committing capital

HOUSTON, Nov. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As more accredited investors turn to oil and gas for diversification, Kevin K. Thibeau, president of Wheeler Resource Recovery since 2014, is outlining five questions investors should ask before backing a secondary-recovery program.

Thibeau brings more than 20 years of industry experience to Wheeler, which focuses on secondary and enhanced-recovery projects in already-producing Texas oil fields.

"Oil and gas can be a strong addition to a portfolio, but only when investors understand exactly what they're buying," said Thibeau. "The right questions up front separate a well-informed investment from a risky one."

The first question is what investment structure is on the table. Direct participation programs, working interest and royalty interest carry different risk, tax and control profiles, and investors should know what their position entitles them to.

The second is the operator's track record. A secondary-recovery program is only as strong as the company running the wells, so investors should ask how many wells that operator has taken through secondary recovery, and with what results.

Third, investors should ask how tax benefits apply to their specific investment. Intangible drilling costs and other deductions can meaningfully change the after-tax picture, but details vary by structure.

Fourth is what returns and timelines are realistic. A credible operator will discuss production timelines, commodity price sensitivity and the full range of outcomes, not just the best case.

Finally, investors should understand the exit path. Direct participation is generally less liquid than public securities, so early-exit options should be clear from the start.

"Every field behaves differently, and no one should promise otherwise," Thibeau added. "Our job is to be candid about risk and show investors the experience and data behind each project."
Wheeler Resource Recovery works only on fields with established production history and documented data. Investors participate directly in the projects, not in Wheeler Resource Recovery's corporate equity.

About Wheeler Resource Recovery

Wheeler Resource Recovery offers accredited investors direct participation in secondary and enhanced recovery projects in already-producing Texas oil fields. The company works alongside Wheeler Operating Corporation, an independent Texas oil and gas operator with roots dating to 1932.

data.title: Bank of Canada to Maintain 2% Inflation Target in Renewed Framework — Update
data.description:
By Paul Vieira 




  OTTAWA--The Bank of Canada and the country's finance department agreed Thursday to renew the central bank's inflation-targeting framework for another five years, with an emphasis on keeping headline inflation at 2%. 



  The central bank was among the first to adopt an inflation-targeting regime in the early 1990s, with a goal to set interest rates to achieve and maintain 2% inflation. According to a joint statement, the government and central bank said the 12-month change in the consumer-price index would act as the beacon for policymakers. 



  "The experience of the past five years has reinforced the value of a clear and credible inflation-targeting framework that provides the bank with the mandate and the flexibility to respond decisively to changing economic conditions," the central bank and finance department said in the statement. 



  Further details will be forthcoming in a speech that Bank of Canada Gov. Tiff Macklem is scheduled to deliver Nov. 24 in Toronto. 



  Unlike the renewal in 2021, references to securing maximum employment were absent in the joint statement. The Federal Reserve has a dual mandate of achieving low, stable inflation and maximum employment through rate policy. 



  "I think it's interesting that there's less emphasis on employment and on core inflation in favor of more emphasis on headline inflation," BMO Capital Markets' economist Shelly Kaushik said after reviewing the joint statement. "I think more focus on headline inflation certainly reads as more hawkish over the short term." 



  In a speech last year, Macklem said officials had no intention of modifying the 2% target. Instead, he said, officials were reviewing whether policymakers have the right gauges of core inflation in place, and whether shelter costs are distorting certain inflation readings. 



  The latest CPI report for Canada indicated that prices rose 3.1% in September from a year ago, while indicators of core inflation--which strips out energy and food prices--remained stable and close to 2%. The Bank of Canada late last month raised its policy rate by a quarter point, to 2.5%, on the expectation that total inflation will remain above 3% until late next year. 



  Economists like David Rosenberg of Rosenberg Research have argued that rate hikes might not be necessary given readings of core CPI, which are meant to focus on underlying price movements by stripping out volatile items. 



  The Bank of Canada faced criticism earlier this decade when inflation ramped up to historically high levels shortly after the peak of the Covid-19 pandemic, forcing Macklem and senior officials to aggressively raise rates, sparking a slowdown in economic activity. 



  The central bank said it thoroughly reviewed that period "and harvested lessons" about setting rate policy. "The bank views the episode not as a failure of the framework's design, but as a challenge to its implementation amid extraordinary global shocks," the joint statement said.

data.title: The 2027 tax brackets are out. See what the standard deduction and SALT tax breaks will be.
data.description:
Andrew Keshner

Income-tax brackets will rise by about 3.2% to reflect rising inflation

It's already time to start thinking about taxes for next year.

The tax brackets at the heart of Americans' income-tax bills will be adjusting at a steeper level in 2027 compared to this year, underscoring inflation's rekindled presence.

Income-tax brackets for 2027 will be climbing by approximately 3.2%, according to IRS numbers. That's after a 2% upward adjustment for this year's taxes.

Meanwhile, the standard deduction is getting an extra $500, climbing to $16,600 for individuals. It will be $33,200 for married couples, up an extra $1,000.

Tax brackets, the standard deduction and approximately 70 other provisions are indexed to rise annually with inflation.

These adjustments have been part of the tax code for decades, protecting households from stumbling too easily into higher tax rates.

The 2027 adjustment is far smaller than the 7% increase in the wake of 2022's white-hot inflation. Still, the IRS's announcement on Thursday is a reminder of the far-reaching impact that's come from higher energy costs in America's standoff with Iran.

Last month, the Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% cost-of-living increase for next year's monthly payments, up from a 2.8% increase this year.

The annual IRS adjustments came days after the midterm elections. High gas prices and rising retail prices weighed heavily on voters, who ousted Republican incumbents across the country.

2027 marks the second full year under the new Republican tax law. The 2025 law prevented tax rates from rising and it increased the amount of the standard deduction, among other things.

The child tax credit climbed to a maximum of $2,200 under the law. It was designed to rise with inflation, and next year the amount will be $2,300 per eligible child, the IRS said.

Some people may have the misconception that households land in just one tax bracket. In fact, most households are subject to several brackets where the rates become progressively steeper.

There are seven tax rates overall, ranging from 10% to 37%.

The new tax brackets will apply to the tax returns that Americans will be filing in 2028 on their 2027 income. That means there's still some time before these numbers affect tax returns.

Nevertheless, understanding the income bands where one tax rate ends and another begins is important for tax planning - especially when everyone's looking to get the most out of their money right now.

Here's what to know for the 2027 tax brackets.

35%                Over $264,550 up to $661,350  $58,480 plus 35% above $264,550

Senior bonuses and standard deduction

Taxpayers age 65 and up are getting an increase on their supplemental standard deduction. It's an extra $2,100 for single filers or $1,700 per person when married.

Don't forget the $6,000 senior bonus, which was created in last year's tax law. The senior bonus can be worth up to $12,000 for married couples. The full deduction is open to individuals with income modified adjusted gross income below $75,000 and $150,000 for joint filers.

Bigger SALT deductions for 2027

The 2025 tax law let households deduct up to four times as much on their state income and local property taxes. That year, the deduction climbed to a maximum of $40,000 from $10,000. Between the years 2026 and 2029, taxpayers claiming this deduction will be able to write off even more.

The increases aren't tied directly to inflation rates. Lawmakers wrote in 1% annual increases between 2026 and 2029.

For 2026, the maximum SALT deduction will be $40,400. The full deduction this year begins to phase out after incomes hit $505,000.

For 2027, the deduction rises to $40,804, and the maximum limit for the full deduction rises to $510,050.

Other inflation adjustments are still coming from the IRS. Retirement-savers should be on the lookout for rules on how much people can contribute to 401(k)s and IRAs.

ROAD TOWN, British Virgin Islands, Nov. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Aura Minerals Inc. (Nasdaq: AUGO) (B3: AURA33) (“Aura” or the “Company”) announced today that its Board of Directors (the “Board”) has declared and approved the payment of a dividend (the “Dividend”) of US$0.72 per common share (approximately US$60.42 million in total). This payment exceeds the minimum distribution foreseen under the Company’s Dividend Policy (the “Dividend Policy”). Under the Dividend Policy, the Company may determine quarterly cash dividends in an aggregate amount equal to 20% of its reported Adjusted EBITDA3 for the relevant three months, less sustaining capital expenditures and exploration capital expenditures for the same period. 

The Dividend will be paid in US dollars on November 27, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on November 18, 2026 (“Record Date”).

Holders of the Company’s Brazilian Depositary Receipts (“BDRs”) as of Record Date will receive US$ 0.24 per BDR (since 1 Aura share is equivalent to 3 BDRs) and are expected to receive payment on or around December 8, 2026, in Brazilian Reais based on the market exchange rate to be disclosed in a future Press Release in advance of its payment date.

As an example, BDR holders will receive:
• Announced Dividend on November 5, 2026: USD 0.24 per BDR
• Exchange Rate, based on closing rate as of November 4, 2026, for USD to Brazilian Reais (BRL): BRL 5.4772 per USD, Dividends Payable to Company BDR Holders would be BRL 1.314528 per BDR. This value will change according to the exchange rate on the day prior to the payment day
• Record Date for Dividend Rights: November 18, 2026
• Payment Date: On or around December 8, 2026

The Dividend is not subject to withholding taxes at the time of payment by the Company.

Rodrigo Barbosa, President & CEO commented, “Q3 2026 was our strongest quarter ever: record production of 95,557 GEO, up 27% quarter-over-quarter and 29% year-over-year, led by a record quarter at Borborema and strong recoveries at Aranzazu and MSG. Nine-month production of 253,131 GEO is the highest in the Company’s history, keeping us on track for our 2026 guidance of 340k–390k GEO. Adjusted EBITDA reached US$236.9 million in the quarter and US$677.4 million year-to-date, already 24% above full-year 2025. Recurring Free Cash Flow (after payment of gold hedges) of US$123.5 million funded US$71 million in dividends and buybacks and US$55 million in expansion capex, with leverage stable at 0.20x. We are pleased to announce a dividend of ~US$60 million, above our Dividend Policy minimum. Era Dorada construction advanced on time and on budget, Almas is delivering on its expansion, and the MSG turnaround is gaining traction. We are executing our strategy: grow production above 600 koz GEO per year, expand resources and reserves, pursue disciplined M&A, and deliver meaningful returns to shareholders. We expect a strong fourth quarter, supported by higher grades at Almas and Apoena, reinforcing our full-year guidance. And there is much more ahead.”

About Aura 360° Mining

Aura is focused on mining in complete terms – thinking holistically about how its business impacts and benefits every one of our stakeholders: our company, our shareholders, our employees, and the countries and communities we serve. We call this 360° Mining.

Aura is a company focused on the development and operation of gold and base metal projects in the Americas. The Company's six operating assets include Minosa gold mine in Honduras; Almas, Apoena, Borborema and MSG gold mines in Brazil; and Aranzazu, a copper, gold, and silver mine in Mexico. Additionally, the Company owns Era Dorada, a gold project in Guatemala; Tolda Fria, a gold project in Colombia; and two projects in Brazil: Matupá, which is under development; and the Carajás copper project in the Carajás region, in the exploration phase.

NU SKIN ENTERPRISES REPORTS THIRD QUARTER EARNINGS

Nu Skin Enterprises Inc. (NYSE: NUS) today announced third quarter revenue within its guidance range.

We continue to see adoption of our Prysm iO platform, including year-to-date growth in revenue from our flagship LifePak nutritional supplements. The Nu Skin Enterprises management team will host a conference call with the investment community today at 5 p.m. (ET). A replay of the webcast will be available on the same page through Nov. 19, 2026.

About Nu Skin Enterprises Inc.

The Nu Skin Enterprises Inc. (NYSE: NUS) family of companies includes Nu Skin and Rhyz Inc. Nu Skin is an intelligent beauty and wellness company, powered by a dynamic affiliate opportunity platform, which operates in nearly 50 markets worldwide. Backed by more than 40 years of scientific research, the company’s products help people look, feel and live their best with brands including Nu Skin® personal care, Pharmanex® nutrition and ageLOC® anti-aging, which includes an award-winning line of beauty and wellness device systems. Formed in 2018, Rhyz is a synergistic ecosystem of consumer, technology and manufacturing companies focused on innovation within the beauty, wellness and lifestyle categories.

data.title: Here's what's driving Iren's stock higher after a brutal selloff
data.description:
By Claudia Assis and Emily Bary

Iren announces a new cloud-computing deal and notes that much of its backlog is tied to 'investment-grade counterparties'

Iren discussed new business deals in its earnings report on Thursday.

Iren investors got a small measure of relief on Thursday when the neocloud company posted results for its September quarter.

Shares of Iren have been among the most pummeled in the technology sector's recent selloff, losing 55% over the past month, including a 17% drop in Thursday's session alone. Like fellow neocloud company CoreWeave (CRWV), Iren (IREN) rents out access to artificial-intelligence computing capacity, making it a focal point for investors worried about the sustainability of data-center spending.

Iren struck a confident tone in its earnings report on Thursday afternoon, noting that its "AI cloud" revenue nearly tripled in the latest quarter to $200 million.

Furthermore, after the quarter ended, the company locked in a five-year contract worth about $22 million per megawatt of computing capacity. The unnamed customer prepaid for 90% of the capital spending required for the chips associated with the deal. Iren also signed a short-term contract worth $40 million per megawatt.

"We own the land, the power and the data centers under all of it, which gives us more ways to fund growth and lets us set its pace," Iren co-CEO Daniel Roberts said in a statement.

Iren shares were up more than 6% in after-hours action on Thursday.

Overall, the company posted quarterly revenue of $228 million, up 66% from just three months earlier. That matched the FactSet consensus view. Iren posted a $263 million net loss, versus a $684 million loss in the June quarter.

The company also offered an update on its financial standing, pointing to $20.6 billion worth of assets. Iren noted its revenue and assets are "underpinned by customer contracts with Nvidia, Microsoft and 13 other customers." Two-thirds of the company's revenue backlog is tied to "investment-grade counterparties," according to the release.

The post-midterms tech rout has been especially vicious toward neocloud companies, but Iren has a few things working in its favor, according to analysts.

For one, despite market jitters about the election of a Democratic governor in Texas who promised a tougher stance on data centers, there could be a time when the state's approved data-center capacity "may end up commanding a scarcity premium," Bernstein analysts said on Wednesday.

And Iren specifically enjoys a diversified customer base as well as a "well calibrated" financial management, the analysts said.

data.title: Bank of Canada to Maintain 2% Inflation Target in Renewed Framework
data.description:
By Paul Vieira 




  OTTAWA--The Bank of Canada and the country's finance department agreed Thursday to renew the central bank's inflation-targeting framework for another five years. 



   The central bank will continue to set rate policy with the aim of achieving and maintaining 2% inflation, as reflected in the 12-month change in the consumer-price index. Central bank officials had previously signaled this was the expected path. 



  "The experience of the past five years has reinforced the value of a clear and credible inflation-targeting framework that provides the bank with the mandate and the flexibility to respond decisively to changing economic conditions," said the Bank of Canada and Canada's Department of Finance in a joint statement. 



  The latest CPI report indicated that prices rose 3.1% in September from a year ago, while indicators of core inflation -- which strips out energy and food prices -- remained stable and close to 2%. The Bank of Canada late last month raised its policy rate by a quarter point, to 2.5%, on the expectation that inflation will remain above 3% until late next year.
